title: AssociativeCommutativePatternMatching.Rule
text: Rule A rule created by @rule or @acrule. Call it on a subject to rewrite it: rule(sub) returns the rewritten term, or nothing if sub does not match.

title: AssociativeCommutativePatternMatching._ceachmatch
text: Tuple{Any, Any} _ceachmatch(pat, sub) Return a vector of the matches of the pattern pat to the subject sub, each a dictionary from wildcard names to their values. The vector is empty if there is no match. Unlike _eachmatch, only commutativity of + and * is used, not associativity.

title: AssociativeCommutativePatternMatching._cmatch
text: Tuple{Any, Any} _cmatch(pat, sub) Return the first match of the pattern pat to the subject sub, or nothing if there is no match. See _ceachmatch.

title: Associativity
text: In an associative operation a slot may match several arguments, combined with the operation, and segments may split the arguments in every way. This can give a combinatorially large number of matches. In a sum there are eight ways to divide three terms between two segments, while for an operation f …

title: Standard order
text: Before matching, the arguments of commutative operations in the subject, and in the parts of the pattern without wildcards, are put in a standard order. So sin(a + b) + ~x matches sin(b + a) + c, but sin(a - b) + ~x does not match sin(b - a) + c. As a consequence, matched values have commutative …

title: Segments
text:
When several segments share the arguments of an operation, only one way of dividing the arguments among them is found, rather than every way: julia> ACPM._ceachmatch(:(f(~~x, ~~y)), :(f(a, b, c)))
1-element Vector{Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any}}:
 Base.ImmutableDict(:y => (), :x => (:a, :b, :c))

title: Slots
text:
The slot ~x matches a single argument, which may itself be an expression: julia> ACPM._cmatch(:(~x + ~y), :(a + sin(b)))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 2 entries:
  :y => :(sin(b))
  :x => :a

julia> ACPM._cmatch(:(~x + ~x), :(a + a))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 1 entry:
  :x => …

title: Default slots
text:
The default slot ~!x matches as ~x does, but when there is no argument to match it binds a default value: 0 within a sum, and 1 within a product, or as an exponent or a denominator. julia> ACPM._cmatch(:(~x + ~!y), :a)
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 2 entries:
  :y => 0
  :x => :a

title: Segments
text:
The segment ~~x matches any number of arguments, including none; ~~~x must match at least one. _match binds the arguments as a vector, _cmatch as a tuple: julia> ACPM._match(:(~x + ~~y), :(a + b + c))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 2 entries:
  :x => :a
  :y => Any[:b, :c]

julia> …

title: Operation slots
text:
A slot in the position of an operation matches the operation of the subject: julia> ACPM._cmatch(:((~F)(~x)), :(sin(a)))
Base.ImmutableDict{Symbol, Any} with 2 entries:
  :x => :a
  :F => :sin

title: Guards
text:
A wildcard may have a guard, a predicate its value must satisfy, written ~x::pred. The match is made only when pred(value) returns true; a guard which returns anything else, or throws an error, rejects the match. julia> ACPM._cmatch(:((~x)^(~n::isinteger)), :(x^2))

title: Rewriting with a match
text: _rewrite(σ, rhs) replaces the wildcards in the template rhs with their values in the match σ. The type of the subject may be given, as _rewrite(σ, rhs, T) or _rewrite(T, σ, rhs); otherwise it is found from the values in σ. For an Expr subject the result is an expression; for a symbolic one …

title: Replacing
text: _replace(ex, pat => rhs) walks through an expression, replacing each part matching pat (with _match) by rhs. The left-hand side may also be a function, to replace an operation, or a variable or expression to replace exactly. julia> ACPM._replace(:(cos(2x)^2 + sin(2x)^2), :(sin(~x)^2 + cos(~x)^2) => …

title: Commutative and associative operations
text: Whether an operation is commutative or associative is decided by the functions iscommutative and isassociative, which are passed the operation of the subject.
